_: SEED CONFIG — copied to your project root as .context-budget.json on first sync, then yours to own. Every ceiling below is a starting point, not a law. Replace each one with a number you can defend from a measurement of YOUR project, and record the derivation in the neighbouring _ key. Re-derive the calibration with: python3 context_budget.py --calibrate
_bytes_per_token: How many bytes of dense markdown cost one token. 2.93 was calibrated on one project by a natural experiment: a commit moved 156,574 B out of CLAUDE.md and the next session's opening context fell 53,520 tokens. Run --calibrate to derive your own; do not inherit this number if you can measure it.
_fixed_harness_tokens: The part of opening context you do NOT control — system prompt, tool schemas, skill listings. Budget your documents as a fraction of this. --calibrate prints it as the regression intercept.
_growth_run: Consecutive non-shrinking measurements before this warns, INDEPENDENT of absolute size. This is the trigger that matters: the 38-session run that motivated this tool never tripped a ceiling, because every individual step was small. It is also the only check that survives someone raising a ceiling to silence a warning.

resident._: Everything your harness injects in full before the session starts. 34,000 B / 2.93 = 11,604 tok = about a third of the 35,700-tok fixed floor. If your CLAUDE.md is bigger than this today, do not raise the ceiling to make it green — that records the problem as the standard.

files._: Auto-loaded in full by Claude Code. Wrap your project's statement of purpose in <!-- budget:protected --> ... <!-- /budget:protected --> and the tool will refuse to let a later compaction remove it. On the project this came from, 32.5% of this file was an index of past failures and 0.5% was what the software is for.

structure.why: Phase 3D says UPDATE the active task. Sessions read that as ADD one; three had accumulated on the project this came from, at lines 7, 10005 and 10218.
if this matches nothing the file has been restructured and every other check here is silently measuring the wrong thing

files._: Phase 0 step 2 orders a read of this file. That instruction is only honest while the file is readable. Set max_lines from what your sessions ACTUALLY read, not from what feels tidy — on the source project the median session read 180 of 26,097 lines and the maximum ever was 334, so 400 sits just above the observed ceiling. The per-line cap exists because a line-count ceiling alone just produces longer lines.

Optional — delete this entry if your project keeps learnings in CLAUDE.md per Phase 3C. A file a pointer sends you to open whole still has a budget: on the source project this reached 215,750 B and was measured, across 51 transcripts, to have been opened exactly once.

synced._: Drift-checked, never size-checked — an adopter may not edit this file, so a size finding would be unactionable. Adjust the canonical path to wherever your methodology checkout lives. Zero local edits means `git diff` in your project shows nothing, so drift is otherwise invisible: on the source project both synced files were 13 and 2 commits behind for 48 days without anyone noticing.
